security_audit.summary: Most Markdown shell-backtick, system-reconnaissance, and documentation URL findings are false positives. Confirmed risks are concentrated in intended OpenRouter network calls, broad .env loading, API-key handling patterns, and local output or log writes. No evidence found of prompt injection, malware intent, or hidden exfiltration beyond the configured external API workflow.

remediation.issue: API keys can be supplied and forwarded through command-line arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the --api-key path, read credentials from environment variables or a secret manager, and avoid passing secrets to child process argv.

remediation.issue: The code searches parent directories for .env files.
remediation.suggestion: Load only an explicit .env path or a documented project-local file, and avoid scanning ancestor directories by default.

remediation.issue: Documentation suggests storing or printing API keys in shell profiles, .env files, and terminal output.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend a secret manager or session-scoped variable, warn against echoing keys, and add clear .env ignore guidance.

remediation.issue: Prompts and generated images are sent to an external API provider.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose external processing clearly and ask users to avoid confidential data unless their policy allows it.

remediation.issue: Review logs may persist sensitive prompt and critique content.
remediation.suggestion: Offer a no-log option, redact sensitive prompts where possible, and document where logs are written.

content.value_statement: Scientific teams need clear diagrams without slow manual drawing. This skill turns detailed prompts into reviewed schematics, pathways, flowcharts, and architecture figures.
actual_capabilities: Generates scientific diagrams from natural language descriptions using OpenRouter API calls.
Supports flowcharts, neural network diagrams, system architectures, circuits, and biological pathways.
Reviews generated images with a Gemini model against document-specific quality thresholds.
Stops early when a diagram meets the selected quality threshold.
Writes versioned image files and a review log for generated figures.
Provides command-line and Python API entry points for diagram generation.
limitations: Requires an OpenRouter API key and network access to generate and review images.
Generated diagrams still need human review for scientific accuracy before publication.
The workflow writes local image files and review logs that may contain prompt details.
It produces raster image outputs, so journal-specific vector formats may need separate conversion.

use_cases.title: Create Manuscript Figures
use_cases.description: Generate first drafts of flowcharts, pathways, and study diagrams for papers and preprints.

use_cases.title: Explain Model Architectures
use_cases.description: Turn neural network and system architecture descriptions into labeled visual diagrams.

use_cases.title: Prepare Grant Visuals
use_cases.description: Create polished workflow and mechanism diagrams for proposals, posters, and slide decks.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Scientific Diagram
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple visual draft.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a scientific schematic for [topic]. Include the main components, clear labels, and a left-to-right flow.

prompt_templates.title: Publication Flowchart
prompt_templates.scenario: Structured study design or participant flow diagram.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a [CONSORT or PRISMA] flowchart for [study]. Include counts, exclusion reasons, group assignments, and final analysis totals.

prompt_templates.title: Technical Architecture Diagram
prompt_templates.scenario: System, neural network, or pipeline architecture.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an architecture diagram for [system]. Show each module, data flow direction, interface labels, and separate input, processing, and output layers.

prompt_templates.title: Publication Quality Refinement
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a journal-ready schematic for [figure purpose]. Use colorblind-safe colors, readable labels, units where needed, and a clean layout for [journal or document type].

output_examples.input: A request for a CONSORT participant flow diagram with screened, excluded, randomized, and analyzed counts.
output_examples.output: A labeled participant flowchart image, versioned iteration files, and a review log with score and critique.

output_examples.input: A request for a transformer encoder-decoder architecture with attention blocks and cross-attention links.
output_examples.output: A structured neural network architecture diagram with labeled encoder, decoder, attention, normalization, and output stages.

output_examples.input: A request for a MAPK pathway from receptor activation to gene transcription.
output_examples.output: A biological pathway schematic with directional arrows, kinase labels, phosphorylation annotations, and distinct component colors.

best_practices: Describe the diagram type, components, labels, and flow direction in the first prompt.
Use environment variables or a secret manager for API keys instead of command-line arguments.
Review generated images, captions, and logs before sharing or submitting work.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague prompts such as only naming the diagram type.
Do not include confidential unpublished data unless external API processing is approved.
Do not commit generated logs, local environment files, or API keys to source control.

faq.question: Does this skill need network access?
faq.answer: Yes. It sends generation and review requests to OpenRouter-hosted models.

faq.question: Can it create diagrams without an API key?
faq.answer: No. The scripts require an OpenRouter API key for AI image generation.

faq.question: What diagram types are supported?
faq.answer: It supports scientific flowcharts, pathways, circuits, system diagrams, block diagrams, and neural network architectures.

faq.question: Are results ready for journal submission?
faq.answer: They are designed for publication quality, but users must verify accuracy, labels, format, and journal requirements.

faq.question: Where are generated files stored?
faq.answer: The scripts write output images, iteration images, and review logs to the chosen output directory.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code support.
